summary: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and also studied with Sonam Germano, William Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Bonn under scholars including Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He taught at several gymnasiums, Trinity College Dublin, and held a professorship at Jena (1875–1901).

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) specializes in religious studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned degrees from Stanford and Harvard, taught at Pomona College (1981–1992), and served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin. He later held professorships in Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Paul Deussen, Hermann Oldenberg, and Georg Bühler, and held positions as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) was an Italian scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore under Giuseppe Bardelli (~1859–1863), and furthered his studies under Albrecht Weber (1863) and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1866).
Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University, attested in 2009, under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) specialized in Japanology and religious studies. Educated at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio University, she studied under Shigeru Gorai and served as a Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge from 1958.

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at the National University of San Marcos and held posts including Professor at the University of Buenos Aires and vice director at the Center of Buddhist Studies.

Carmen Meinert (born 1969) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001 and has held research fellowships at the University of Hamburg and Ruhr University Bochum.

Carol Breckenridge (1942–2009) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and later held an academic post at the University of Chicago.

Carol S. Anderson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and became Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff (born 1959) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under David P. Jackson and Geshe Thubten Ngawang, earned her Magister at the University of Hamburg, and served as a visiting professor there from 2018 to 2025.

Carola S. Carstens is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She held a position at Rice University (1998–1999) and completed her doctorate in philosophy at the University of Hamburg by 2006.
Carole M. Cusack (born 1962) is a religious studies scholar. She studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan (born 1969) is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Colgate University and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, joining the University of Colorado Boulder as an assistant professor in 2001.

Caroline Humphrey (born 1943) works in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. She studied at Girton College, Leeds, and Cambridge (PhD under Edmund Ronald Leach), later serving as a fellow and university lecturer at Cambridge (1978–2010).

Caroline Rhys Davids (1857–1942) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at University College London, she served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society (1907–1942) and lectured at Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and worked as a graduate teaching associate there and as a visiting lecturer at Denison University.

Carson T. Schütze (born 1968) is a linguist who completed his studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology between 1992 and 1997, taking up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1997.
